corrections_applied: See contracts/CHANGELOG.md and docs/pathways/DECISION_LOG.md section N and docs/pathways/PHASE4_DECISION_ENGINE_SPEC_V1.md. Extends the 1.1.0-phase3e-discovery-calibrated policy with the machine-readable parameters the Phase 4 engine (src/lib/engine) actually reads -- the human-readable string fields below are retained verbatim as documentation, but every number/threshold/mapping the engine uses to decide qualification and ordering now also exists as a structured value so the engine never has to parse English policy prose. No public numeric score exists at any layer.
multiplier_policy: Use only the largest applicable multiplier per scoring group, never multiply multipliers. Priority when several are eligible for the same group: primary Discovery reason (1.75) > any selected family priority mapped to that group (1.50, unranked -- any one qualifying selection establishes it) > desired_primary_change mapped to that group (1.15) > default (1.00). desired_primary_change's multiplier never satisfies the display gate's primary/priority link requirement on its own -- only a primary-reason-linked or family-priority-linked positive group does.
group_aggregation: Per candidate and group: collect all positive score effects from currently-triggered (non-RETIRED) rules in that group for that model, keep the largest; collect all negative effects, keep the most negative; add those two; apply the one group multiplier; clamp the result to group_bounds [-6,6]. Sum every group's clamped contribution onto baseline (50); clamp the total to score_bounds [0,100]. This is the internal score -- never shown publicly. Grouping prevents repeated schedule/flexibility-shaped questions from accumulating as independent evidence, and evaluation must be independent of JSON rule array order (src/lib/engine iterates all triggered rules and only then aggregates by group/model, never short-circuiting on order).
display_gate_description: A normal candidate qualifies only when: discovery_enabled is true; it is not objectively excluded; its internal score is strictly greater than 50; at least two distinct scoring groups have a final positive (>0) contribution for that candidate; and at least one of those positive groups is a group that the family's primary Discovery reason maps to, OR a group that at least one of the family's selected family priorities maps to (desired_primary_change's own group mapping does not satisfy this link on its own -- see multiplier_policy). Baseline score alone (an internal score of 50 with zero positive groups) never qualifies -- one click alone must never create a recommendation. The ONLY exception to the two-group/link requirement is B01's explicit stay-current continuity statement (docs/pathways/PHASE4_DECISION_ENGINE_SPEC_V1.md section 12): when a real (non-NOT_ENROLLED, non-UNKNOWN/missing) current_education_model exists and school_change_preference is STAY_CURRENT, B01 may qualify on its internal score alone (still requiring score > 50), even with only one positive group. This exception is general (keyed only on those two fields), never keyed on a persona or profile identity.
sorting: Descending internal score first; ties (including a deliberate educational tie such as B03 vs B06) broken by ascending stable base-model ID string (B01 < B02 < ... < B09) -- never by cost, never by a hidden preference for one delivery format over another. This tie-break existing is not itself evidence that the lower-ID model is educationally superior.

diversity.description: A ceiling of 2, never a quota to fill. Sort qualifying candidates by internal score descending (stable ID ascending tie-break), select the highest; then prefer the highest-scoring qualifying candidate from a DIFFERENT model family. Only for a family listed in same_family_multi_display_families (currently just HOMESCHOOL, i.e. B08+B09) may a second same-family candidate display instead, and only when both independently qualify -- this is a general per-family policy flag, never a persona-keyed exception. The VIRTUAL family (B03/B06) and IN_PERSON family (B02/B05) always dedupe to one representative under this policy. Cost is never used to choose the representative.

legacy_safe_mappings_note: primary_reason_groups' TRAVEL/ARTS/FAMILY_INVOLVEMENT entries were valid discovery_reasons/primary_discovery_reason selections before Phase 3F.1 removed them from DISC_006's new-entry option set (contracts/question-bank.json grade_band_allowed_values) without aliasing or removing them, so a historical primary_discovery_reason could still literally carry one; mapped to the group their content most directly concerns (schedule for TRAVEL/ARTS since both are the same schedule-conflict family as ATHLETICS/SCHEDULE_FLEXIBILITY, family_role for FAMILY_INVOLVEMENT). ADVANCED_COURSES/COLLEGE_ADVANCEMENT/CREDIT_RECOVERY/CURRENT_SCHOOL_CONCERN/DIFFERENT_ENVIRONMENT/SMALLER_ENVIRONMENT/ENVIRONMENT_CONCERN can no longer be produced by discovery_reasons itself (Phase 3F.1 aliases them away in effective answers -- contracts/legacy-aliases.json question_value_aliases.discovery_reasons), but primary_discovery_reason (DISC_007) is not itself alias-normalized, so an older stored raw answer could in principle still carry one of these literal legacy values; each is mapped to the exact same group(s) as its canonical alias target (ADVANCED_COURSES/COLLEGE_ADVANCEMENT -> ACADEMIC_ACCELERATION -> academic; CREDIT_RECOVERY -> ACADEMIC_SUPPORT -> academic+support_structure; CURRENT_SCHOOL_CONCERN/DIFFERENT_ENVIRONMENT/SMALLER_ENVIRONMENT/ENVIRONMENT_CONCERN -> BETTER_FIT_ENVIRONMENT -> context) so the engine never treats old data as unmapped or maps it to a different group than its canonical replacement would.
unmapped_priority_behavior: AFFORDABILITY is feasibility-only and is deliberately absent from family_priority_groups -- it establishes no educational-alignment multiplier for any group (the cost group itself is never scored by any rule, so this is belt-and-suspenders, not merely documentation). EXPLORING/OTHER/UNKNOWN values across discovery_reasons, family_priorities and desired_primary_change are deliberately absent and establish no multiplier. ACADEMIC_QUALITY, ACCREDITATION and DIPLOMA (family_priorities) were retired entirely at Phase 3E/3F (contracts/legacy-aliases.json question_value_removals) and do not prove generic-model superiority.
state_availability_policy: REV_STATE_AVAILABILITY is attached engine-natively (src/lib/engine/considerations.ts), not by a single JSON rule: it applies to any QUALIFYING candidate whose base model ID is in material_review_mapping.REV_STATE_AVAILABILITY, regardless of the specific reason that candidate qualified. This reflects that any state-dependent remote/home direction always carries an unverified-availability consideration once it is actually being shown, not only when a specific travel/relocation answer was given.
postprocess_rules: Any qualifying B08/B09 carries REV_STATE_HOMESCHOOL via rule HOME_001 (fires on homeschool_interest, which is required for B08/B09 to ever qualify).

Any qualifying candidate in material_review_mapping.REV_STATE_AVAILABILITY's scope (B03/B04/B06/B08/B09) carries REV_STATE_AVAILABILITY -- see state_availability_policy above; this is engine-native, not a rules.json rule.
Qualifying B05/B06 plus cost_preference = PREFER_TUITION_FREE carries REV_COST_ALIGNMENT via rule COST_ALIGNMENT_REVIEW (empty score_effects; never infer an exact budget).

B10 cannot be a displayed or qualifying candidate under any version -- excluded architecturally (taxonomy.json reachability_status EXCLUDED plus contract validation plus the engine's own candidate universe, which never includes B10 at all).
Do not infer blanket incompatibility when a specific school capability has not been verified.
Other/unknown grade keeps universal questions and neutral review; do not force an age-derived grade band.

For K-4 suppress college/credit/athletic eligibility report modules and use foundational enrichment wording (a future Phase 5/Report concern; the engine itself simply never activates those signals for ELEMENTARY grade_band since no rule condition matches).
For middle grades, college-related opportunity stage is LONGER_TERM_EXPLORATION; for HS it remains EXPLORE_NOT_ELIGIBLE (taxonomy.json opportunity default_status; a future Report concern).

DEC-H2 (Phase 3E) and DEC-N (Phase 4): cost_preference is PRACTICAL FEASIBILITY context, never a base-model score input -- a preference for tuition-free options must not itself raise a tuition-free model's score or be presented as proof it is the better educational fit, and must never lower a private model's educational score either. REV_COST_ALIGNMENT is the only mechanism by which cost reaches a candidate.
